title: Efficacy of sapropterin dihydrochloride (tetrahydrobiopterin, 6R-BH4) for reduction of phenylalanine concentration in patients with phenylketonuria: a phase III randomised placebo-controlled study
authors: Levy HL, Milanowski A, Chakrapani A, Cleary M, Lee P, Trefz FK, et al.
population: Patients with phenylketonuria, mean age 20 years, mean baseline blood phenylalanine 843 and 888 umol/L in the two groups
funder: Lead sponsor BioMarin Pharmaceutical (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00104247). The funding statement of the article was not readable; the archived article page showed only the summary and affiliations.
authorConflicts: One author (A. Dorenbaum) was affiliated with BioMarin Pharmaceutical and two (J. D. Bebchuk, H. Christ-Schmidt) with Statistics Collaborative.
result: 42 patients were assigned sapropterin 10 mg/kg once daily and 47 placebo. After 6 weeks mean blood phenylalanine fell by 236 (SD 257) umol/L with sapropterin and rose by 3 (SD 240) umol/L with placebo (p<0.0001). A reduction of 30% or more occurred in 18 of 41 (44%) versus 4 of 47 (9%): absolute difference 35 percentage points, number needed to treat about 3 over 6 weeks.
